verdicts.reasoning: Verified on disk; the claim's elided quote is faithful and both fragments sit on line 27. KICKOFF lines 1309-1311 re-list every field the skill's Output section already fixes — before/after numbers, the same three parenthetical metrics in the same order (response time, throughput, resource use), bottlenecks found, fixes applied, validating evidence, and alert thresholds phrased with the same rationale ("keep the gains from regressing" / "so gains don't regress"). The path is indeed hardcoded in the skill at line 27, so on a naive reading it is duplicated. The cross-step coordination the claim invokes is real and I verified it in KICKOFF at lines 1301-1302: "Run them in this order; both write under `docs/global/ops/monitoring/`, so do not overlap them." The operator needs the concrete path visible to honor that non-overlap instruction against the following sre-engineer/monitoring-expert block. Keep. Low severity — this is a KEEP verdict, not a defect.

verdicts.evidence: performance-engineer.md:27 — "If the bottleneck is infra-wide or capacity-related rather than app-code-level, hand dashboard/capacity follow-through to `monitoring-expert` (infra lane) instead of continuing app-level profiling."
verdicts.reasoning: Verified verbatim as the final sentence of line 27. KICKOFF lines 1312-1314 reproduce it with the same trigger condition (infra-wide or capacity-related vs. app-level), the same handoff target (monitoring-expert), the same payload (dashboard and capacity follow-through), and the same stop instruction (rather than continuing to profile app code). I tested the strongest counter-argument — that cross-skill handoff is orchestration and therefore load-bearing under the ordering/parallelism carve-out. It fails: the carve-out covers dispatch ordering the operator decides up front, whereas this condition can only be evaluated by the agent mid-run, after profiling, and the skill already encodes that exact conditional gate itself. So it is the skill's own hard rule restated, per the rubric. High severity: three lines of near-verbatim gate text with a named downstream agent, the highest drift risk in the block.
